tierWindow.goal: Own your development within the university system: direct your own learning as a self-regulated process, apply marking criteria to appraise and raise your own work, and turn feedback into a cycle that feeds forward.
tierWindow.cognitiveDemand: Analysis, evaluation, synthesis and self-regulation; articulating and justifying your own judgements, and planning your own development.
tierWindow.taskComplexity: Ill-defined and multi-step; your own work across modules, with competing demands you prioritise and standards you set for yourself.
tierWindow.autonomy: Low scaffolding; you set the standard, critique your own work, and decide what to carry forward. Feedback invites and extends rather than confirms.

decidedValue.priorExperienceAnchor: Assumes the learner already understands what learning, assessment and feedback are at university (the introductory tier) and can work with the system and manage their own study (the intermediate tier). This course assumes that grounding and turns to ownership: becoming a self-regulating learner who directs, appraises and develops their own academic practice.

subThemes.label: Self-regulated learning: taking control of your own learning by setting goals, monitoring your behaviour, and evaluating your performance
Self-regulated learning as a three-phase process: forethought, performance and evaluation
Becoming a self-regulating learner: monitoring your own performance and amending a strategy that is not working
Marking criteria as a tool you apply to your own work, not only a measure tutors use on it
Self and peer assessment: applying the criteria yourself to judge and raise the standard of your work
The feedback cycle: review, interpret, articulate and apply, run as a self-directed loop
Making effective use of feedback: a growth mindset that turns comments into action in your next piece of work

decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has three short lessons. First, directing your own learning: self-regulated learning as a process you drive. Second, setting your own standard: using marking criteria to appraise your own work. Third, making feedback feed forward: the feedback cycle run as a self-directed loop. Work through them in order; each builds on the one before.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the three lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview:
This course is about owning your development as a learner. You already know how university learning, assessment and feedback work. The step now is to take charge of them: to direct your own learning, judge your own work against the standard, and make feedback change what you do next.

By the end you will be able to direct your learning as a self-regulated process, apply marking criteria to appraise and raise your own work, and turn feedback into a cycle that feeds forward. These are the habits that mark out a self-regulating learner, and they carry straight into professional practice.
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: direct your own learning, apply marking criteria to your own work, feed feedback forward.

practiceConnection.academic: Owning your development is what independent academic work rests on. Every project you plan and monitor, every draft you judge against the criteria before you submit it, every piece of feedback you act on rather than file away, is this ownership at work. The same self-regulation is what employers and research both expect of a graduate.

grounding.note: W-OPEN states the three course outcomes and why they matter (AL-5)

decidedValue.whereNextBody: From here the habits widen. The reflective-practice pathway takes the evaluation and feedback work deeper; researching and academic writing put self-regulation, criteria and feedback to work on larger pieces. Each is a place to keep owning your development.
decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Owning your development is no longer an idea but something you can do. You can direct your own learning as a self-regulated process of forethought, performance and evaluation. You can apply marking criteria to appraise your own work and raise its standard. And you can run feedback as a cycle that feeds forward into your next task. Look back at the confidence check: comparing where you started with where you are now shows how far this has moved.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, owning your development is something you practise in every module. Each task you plan and monitor, each draft you judge against the criteria, each piece of feedback you turn into action, is self-regulation at work. It is also what professional life rewards: the graduate who directs their own learning, judges their own work, and improves from feedback is the one who keeps growing.
